Enum Class SessionFixationPolicy

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<SessionFixationPolicy>
org.springframework.security.extension.property.SessionFixationPolicy
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<SessionFixationPolicy>, Constable
public enum SessionFixationPolicy extends Enum<SessionFixationPolicy>
Strategy that describes how the security framework should mitigate session-fixation attacks by changing the session identifier after authentication.

The values mirror Spring Security's SessionFixationProtectionStrategy options and are typically used by the HTTP security configuration to determine which SessionAuthenticationStrategy should be installed.

Since:
3.0.0
Author:
[@Loong Wan](https://github.com/loong10k)

  • Enum Constant Details

    • CHANGE_SESSION_ID

      public static final SessionFixationPolicy CHANGE_SESSION_ID
      Specifies that the Servlet container-provided session fixation protection should be used. When a session authenticates, the Servlet 3.1 method HttpServletRequest#changeSessionId() is called to change the session id and retain all session attributes.

      Using this option in a Servlet 3.0 or older container results in an IllegalStateException.

    • MIGRATE_SESSION

      public static final SessionFixationPolicy MIGRATE_SESSION
      Specifies that a new session should be created and the session attributes from the original HttpSession should be retained.

    • NEW_SESSION

      public static final SessionFixationPolicy NEW_SESSION
      Specifies that a new session should be created, but the session attributes from the original HttpSession should not be retained.

    • NONE

      public static final SessionFixationPolicy NONE
      Specifies that no session fixation protection should be enabled. This may be useful when other mechanisms for protecting against session fixation are already in place (for example when the application container provides its own protection). Otherwise, this option is not recommended.
